CATERPILLAR CRAWL - a RetroStone VC game for Windows
(c) 2026 Pierre-Louis Boyer (8BCraft). Code MIT, art/music/sound CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: see LICENSE-caterpillarcrawl.txt.

A round green caterpillar crawls around a garden bed munching leaves. Each
leaf makes it longer; bump into the wooden frame, a stone or your own tail
and the run is over. Flowers are worth bonus points, a berry slows time for
a moment. Twelve leaves and it spins a cocoon and flutters off as a
butterfly: on to the next garden, with new obstacles and a little more
speed. Medals at 20, 45, 90 and 150, and your best score is kept.

Run CaterpillarCrawl.exe. No installation needed (SDL2 is built in).

Controls                  Gamepad (SNES layout)      Keyboard
  turn                      D-pad                      arrows
  start                     A (or Start, the D-pad)    X or Enter
  pause / resume            Select (or Start in a run) Backspace or Esc
  players 2-4 join          A on their pad, on the title (B leaves)
  back to the title         A (or Select) on the game over
  touch / mouse             swipe to turn (keep the finger down to steer on); a tap starts

Turns are remembered: press up then left quickly and the caterpillar makes
a U-turn in two steps. It never turns straight back into itself.

With 2 to 4 players it is a battle in the garden bed: everyone grows as they
crawl, touching any body or the frame puts you out, and the last one still
crawling wins the round. First to 3 round wins takes the match.

F11 or Alt+Enter: fullscreen. F12: screenshot. Close the window to quit.
Options: CaterpillarCrawl.exe --scale 4 --fullscreen
The best score is saved in caterpillarcrawl.srm next to the exe.
